# From a pull request review

After a Cursor plugin install, the short command loop is [plugins/crav1/README.md](../plugins/crav1/README.md).

It is the same command family as `$crav1-open-pr` and `$crav1-merge-pr`. `$crav1-open-pr` may name this command and does not run it. `$crav1-merge-pr` does not run it.

## First prompt

```text
$crav1-review-pr
https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<n>

Read the diff. Do not edit. Do not run the tests. Do not merge.
```

On Azure DevOps, the review lists, checks and posts threads with `scripts/ado_threads.py`. It reads the az output safely on Windows, so a Swedish or other non-ASCII character in a comment no longer breaks the listing, and a re-review is always posted as a new thread.

## Steps

| Phase | You | Agent |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Which pull request | Named it by number or URL | Asks which one and stops when none was named. Does not pick the newest |
| Comment as posted | Confirm the comment, or paste it | When the PR note has a drafted comment with nothing posted after it, first finds the posted comment on the pull request (read-only) or asks you to paste it, saves it word for word, and compares it with the draft (1.67.0) |
| Read | — | Reads the diff, the spec, and the pull request body, and whether a linter is required and green. When the slug has `plan.md`, also reads the plan and `verify.md`. When the slug has no `plan.md` or `tasks.md`, reads the test results that pull request's own pipeline already recorded. Does not edit. Does not run the tests |
| Fixed checks | Open the PR note when you want them | Written to the PR note's kit record, not the chat (1.113.0). The same 7 checks every run (1.95.0), one line each even when clean: spec and plan match, tests, secrets, infrastructure access per environment, environment parity, spec wording a bug touches, and merge order against the other open branches. Each line says `ok`, the finding ids, or `n/a` with a reason, so two runs on the same branch cover the same ground |
| Must be true before ship | Open the PR note when you want them | In the kit record. Each miss is its own finding. Three lines: what is off, what could happen, and the decision (ship, fix, or drop). Any fix or drop means the review does not say ship. An outside-the-kit note and a recorded-test note are info. They do not block ship |
| Lane | — | Names the lane in the kit record and does not start it. Spec miss → Specify. Plan miss → Plan, only when that slug has `plan.md`. Verify miss, a file the plan already named but the diff lacks, or a red or missing linter → Build. Body mismatch → rewrite the pull request body, not a new spec |
| Suggestions | Open the PR note when you want them | In the kit record. Style, patterns, and practices the repo already wrote down, plus dead code, or a name that hides what the code does. They do not block ship. A secret in the diff is a first-section fix |
| Paste-ready comment | Copy it, or wait for the post question | Says the verdict in the chat, then one Markdown block you can paste into the pull request as one comment: a short opening, then Blockers, Bugs, Tests to add with this PR, and A question, each point starting with a link to its file and line. Showing it posts nothing |
| Post | Post, I'll post it myself, or do not post | Asks once whether to post under your own account, naming the vote. On yes, posts the block as one comment, sets that vote and saves the posted text |
| Stop | Glance | A clean review says so and stops. It does not merge. It never resolves a thread without your yes |

## What it checks

- **Spec.** The diff does not add product behavior the spec never asked for, and it does not leave out something the spec said must be true.
- **Plan.** Only when the slug has `plan.md`. The files and the checks named on the plan tasks are in the diff. A task that never named a needed file or check is a plan miss.
- **Verify.** Only when the slug has `plan.md`. It quotes `verify.md` when that file is already on the branch. It says so when the file is missing. It does not run the tests.
- **Pull request body.** The description matches that same scope, not wider or narrower than the diff. `$crav1-open-pr` writes a short body (summary, one line per task, Verified, work item), checked task by task: each task line against the diff, and each change in the diff against a task line. An older format A body is still checked bullet by bullet: each Changes bullet against the lines it links, and each change in the diff against a bullet. A body mismatch stays on the pull request. This command does not open a new spec for it.
- **Linter.** A linter or checker covers the code in the diff, and that check is required and green. If none exists, or it exists but is not required, or it is required and red, the decision is fix. This command does not install a linter.
- **Secrets.** A secret in the diff is a fix. The review names the path and does not print the secret.

## Built outside the kit

When the slug has no `plan.md` or `tasks.md`, the pull request was built outside the kit. It does not report a missing `verify.md`.

Instead of `verify.md`, it reads the test results that pull request's own pipeline already recorded.

It names `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` as the next step after the pull request merges, to bring its changes into the spec and `docs/system/`.

A pull request that has a plan keeps the plan and `verify.md` checks in the section above.

## Paste-ready comment

- Starts with one short, plain line, such as "I've looked through the PR and run it through my checks. This is what I found:". No greeting, no praise.
- Has the sections **Blockers**, **Bugs**, **Tests to add with this PR**, and **A question** (or **Questions**). A section with nothing in it is left out.
- Starts each point with a link to its file and line on the pull request's source branch, then the explanation as an indented paragraph. A point with no file line starts with a link to the pull request overview, or to a branch for a merge-order point.
- Gives at most one fix per point, with no "or …" and nothing after the fix.
- Has no follow-ups, no table, no closing line, no HTML, and no kit details (no spec paths, skill names, or numbering that only the chat explains).
- Is in English, unless you ask for another language for that comment.

The kit never suggests a rebase.

```markdown
I've looked through the PR and run it through my checks. This is what I found:

### Blockers

- [PR 42 overview](https://dev.azure.com/contoso/orders/_git/orders-api/pullrequest/42)

  **No required build:** I can't find any required build or check on the PR, so no green build or lint protects the merge. Could we add a build policy?

### Bugs

- [functions/orders-sync/store.py, line 401](https://dev.azure.com/contoso/orders/_git/orders-api?path=/functions/orders-sync/store.py&version=GBfeature/orders-retry-table&line=401&lineEnd=401&lineStartColumn=1&lineEndColumn=1)

  `RowKey` is random for every write, so a resent file adds a new row instead of an upsert. Maybe the key could be built from the file name and revision number?

### Tests to add with this PR

- [functions/orders-sync/store.py, line 401](https://dev.azure.com/contoso/orders/_git/orders-api?path=/functions/orders-sync/store.py&version=GBfeature/orders-retry-table&line=401&lineEnd=401&lineStartColumn=1&lineEndColumn=1)

  An idempotency test: the same file name and revision number twice should give one row.
```

On GitHub the same link is `https://github.com/contoso/orders-api/blob/feature/orders-retry-table/functions/orders-sync/store.py?plain=1#L401`. The full rules are in the skill's `references/comment-layout.md`.

## What the chat shows (1.113.0)

A plain `$crav1-review-pr <pr>` shows only the review you can post: the verdict, the paste-ready block, one line `Kit record: <PR note path>`, and the post question. That kit record (the 7 check lines, findings with lanes, info notes, suggestions, follow-ups, the next step after merge) is saved in the PR note.

The review still reads as plain review comments and never mentions the mail, the kit or the specs. That section is also saved next to the PR note, with `-context` added to its name, and the PR note links it.

## Comment style

The block, every posted comment, and every re-review reply use the style Thomas and Rhea agreed on 2026-10-12, tightened in 1.66.0.

- Your own first-person voice, friendly, so the author never feels criticized.
- A vague source, such as "me and my checks". It never names a tool, a bot, or the kit.
- A short, plain opening that may vary slightly. Never praise, a greeting by name, or thanks.
- Soft wording with the same facts: "I noticed…", "Would it be worth adding a test that…?" One fix per point.
- The pull request description is read first. A choice it calls deliberate is not raised as a fault, unless it contradicts something written in the repo. A task line in the short body states what that task is meant to do. With an older format A body it is per point: the why on the Changes bullet that links those lines, and anything its Not in this PR section names as left out. Otherwise it becomes a follow-up.

## Post it

1. The block is posted as **one comment**, with no inline threads: on GitHub as the body of one review, on Azure DevOps as one thread.
2. The vote follows the verdict:

It never rejects. Follow-ups are never posted.

## Comment as posted (1.67.0)

So the PR note keeps both texts in its history, each word for word in a code fence (1.97.0; before that, a separate follow-ups note did):

- `## Comment as drafted, <date>`: the paste-ready block of each review, in a four-backtick fence. only a review that ends with a new block adds one; recording the comment as posted (`comment-posted`, `newest-comment`, a paste) never does. the heading is always plain, on a re-review too; a re-review tag goes only on the `## Kit record` heading.
- `## Comment as posted, <date> (by <name>)`: what the reviewers see, with one line saying where it came from (read from the PR thread, pasted in chat, or posted from this review), which draft it was compared with, and which `Description as of` section of the PR note the review read. `by` is your name as the host shows it.

**How it gets the posted text.** When the review posts on your yes, it saves the text the host returns at once. When you pick **I'll post it myself**, say "posted" when it's up, or run `$crav1-review-pr orders-api 42 comment-posted`. Every later run on that pull request also checks first. It looks read-only for your review or comment on the pull request (GitHub reviews and conversation comments; Azure DevOps top-level threads, or your reply in the earlier thread), posted after the draft, that matches it. One match: it asks you to confirm. Several: it lists them, and you may pick more than one. None: it says so in one line and goes on, since you may not have posted it yet. No `gh` or `az` session, or nothing found after `comment-posted`: it asks you to paste it. An edit on the host later adds a new section ending `, edited`; the earlier one stays.

**Comparing.** Points are paired by their link and title. The chat lists them as drafted, changed, not in the posted comment, or added. A drafted point you left out stays in the note as a bullet ending `(Not in the posted comment, <date>; still open.)`. A cut question keeps its `Asked on the PR:` line, with the mark added. A question you added gets an `Asked on the PR:` line.

`````markdown
- `src/orders/retry_store.py`, line 9: an idempotency test for the row key. (Not in the posted comment, 2026-10-19; still open.)

## Comment as posted, 2026-10-19 (by Alex Doe)
Read from the PR thread: https://github.com/contoso/orders-api/pull/42#issuecomment-1001. Draft compared: 2026-10-19. Description reviewed: as of 2026-10-18 (PR note).

````markdown

### Bugs

- [src/orders/retry_store.py, line 9](https://github.com/contoso/orders-api/blob/feat/orders-retry/src/orders/retry_store.py?plain=1#L9)

````
`````

Secrets are removed and named by kind, and the source line says `Verbatim except: <kind> removed.`

For bots: `comment-posted` records only, `newest-comment` takes the newest match, and `skip-comment-record` skips the step.

## Re-review

A resolved thread whose problem is still there is flagged `resolved but still open`.

Lines are never copied from the earlier review.

## Specs in another repo (1.65.0)

The specs often live in their own repo (`orders-specs`) and the code pull requests in others (`orders-api` on Azure DevOps, merging into `develop`).

- **From the specs repo**, for a pull request in a repo listed in `docs/system/repos.md`: `$crav1-review-pr orders-api 71`, or the pull request URL. The repo is matched on its `URL` cell.
- **With both repos open** in one workspace: the folder with `docs/specs/` is the specs repo, and the folder whose remote matches the pull request is the code repo.

It reads the pull request from the host (`gh` or `az`, read-only), and the spec, plan and `verify.md` from the specs repo's working tree. The spec is found by the head branch in its `Synced at` lines, Match `Branch:` list or task `(branch: orders-api …)` parts. A code pull request whose spec has a `plan.md` gets the full checks, not the outside-the-kit note. When the spec spans several repos, another repo's part is not a miss; an `I3` info note lists it with the Branches line.

A GitHub diff comes from `gh pr diff`. An Azure DevOps diff comes from the code repo's checkout (`../orders-api`).

1. **Fetch only the PR's two branches (Recommended)**: fetches just those two branches there; nothing is checked out or committed.
2. **Use what's on disk**: diffs the copies there and says how old they are and that newer commits may be missed.
3. **Stop**: you fetch and rerun.

A bot passes `fetch-pr-branches`, `use-disk` or `stop-pr-review`.

Run from the code repo with the specs repo not open, it finds the specs repo next door (`../orders-specs`, by its `repos.md` row), writes the notes there, never commits them, and names the full path.

## PR note (1.65.0)

Every review saves the pull request's title and description as a **PR note** in the specs repo, so specs can link to it locally: `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-pr-orders-api-71.md`, filed by the pull request's created date, `kind: pull request`, `source: PR 71 dev.azure.com/contoso/orders/orders-api`. A later review reuses it; when the description changed, it appends a `## Description as of <date>` section and never removes the earlier text. Pull requests made by `$crav1-open-pr` get one too. `$crav1-merge-pr` writes or updates it after a merge, and `$crav1-add-to-spec code-change orders-api PR 71` uses it. Code-change notes link it with `pr_note:`.

## Follow-ups and the PR record (1.97.0)

The kit record in the PR note lists them; the chat only says `Kit record: <path>`. Everything the review raises goes into the PR note's shared `## PR record`, one line per point, in the merge-safe format of `crav1-add-to-spec` `references/pr-record.md`:

```text
- Point: src/orders/retry_store.py:9 | open | Sam Lee | from review-pr 2026-10-19 | An idempotency test for the row key
- Point: src/orders/retry.py | follow-up | - | from review-pr 2026-10-19 | Split the retry policy into its own module later
- Point: general | waiting on Sam Lee | Sam Lee | asked; from review-pr 2026-10-19 | Is the cut-off local time?
```

A finding is `open`, a follow-up is `follow-up`, a question is `waiting on <author>` tagged `asked`, and a drafted point you cut from the posted comment gets `not posted <date>`. A re-review reads the record first, sets a point the code now addresses to `done <short sha>`, and never deletes a line. The same record is read and written by [`$crav1-pr-status`](from-pr-status.md) (where every thread stands), `$crav1-add-to-spec pr<n> all` and `$crav1-merge-pr` (which stops on `Ready: no`). The follow-ups come back through the existing note flow: [`$crav1-ado-sync`](from-ado-sync-suggest-features.md) reads `follow-up` Points as open items, and the spec that takes one adds itself to the note's `used_by`. Notes are never absorbed. The note is not committed; `$crav1-finalize-commit` does that.

Before 1.97.0 the follow-ups lived in a separate `docs/notes/YYYY-MM/review-pr-[<repo>-]<n>-follow-ups.md`. A review still reads one and says to run `$crav1-add-to-spec migrate-formats`, which moves it into the PR note ([install](install.md)).

## Shared pull-request steps (1.158.0)

`$crav1-review-pr` resolves, reads and checks the state of the pull request the same way as open-pr, merge-pr and pr-status, as [Shared pull-request steps](reference/pr-common.md) says.

## What does not get written

No `spec.md` edit. No `plan.md` edit.

## After

On an outside pull request, the last line names `$crav1-refresh-system-notes` and the review does not run it.

```text
$crav1-merge-pr
<the same pull request number or URL>
```

Reference page: [review-pr](reference/skills/crav1-review-pr.md)

## A branch with no pull request (1.80.0)

`$crav1-review-pr branch feature/orders-retry` reviews a branch before any pull request exists. `$crav1-review-pr branch` takes the current branch, and `$crav1-review-pr branch orders-api feature/orders-retry` a repo from `repos.md`.

It diffs from the base with local git only, never fetching. The base comes from the spec's Match `Branch:` entry and its `(into …)` or `(spec branch)` marker, then the repo's `Merges into`, then the default branch, and the review shows it: `Base: develop (Merges into). Merge-base: 1a2b3c4. Remote copy: 2 days.` With no base it asks once, with up to 4 likely bases and Other; a headless run stops and says to name one.

The checks are those of a pull request review: spec, plan, `verify.md`, the secret rule, `F#` findings and suggestions. When the base moved on, it suggests merging the base into the branch, never a rebase.

The run ends as [How a run ends](reference/run-ending.md) says: Run next, never a `Next:` line. While the PR note is uncommitted, Run next is `Commit the PR note:` with `$crav1-finalize-commit`, then `Then push the specs repo:` with `git push`, each command alone in its code span. `Waiting:` only when a step is blocked, and `Uncommitted:` in chat when files changed and are not committed.

`ado_threads.py` takes the Azure DevOps organization, project and repository from the code repo's git remote, so posting the review thread no longer fails with 404 when they are not passed. `--org`, `--project` and `--repo` still override.
